## Glossary

**adapter module**  
types.ts interface + client/<provider>.ts factories + index.ts wiring; app code imports only the exported adapter.

**adapters**  
Class: provider adapter modules exposing one interface over provider implementations, wired with makeAdapterRouter/Registry.

**app-events**  
Class: the emitAppEvent side-effect bus, makeAppEvent handlers, their email/WebSocket/observe handoffs and commit deferral.

**AppEvent**  
Model recording emitted events (upserted by envelope id) with actor, source and payload.

**AppEventName**  
Typed union of event names, declared with their payloads and registrations in apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts.

**circuit breaker**  
A subscription auto-disables after 5 consecutive failed events.

**createS3Client**  
Provider factory building the memoized S3-backed StorageClient from typed config.

**db.onCommit**  
Defers a callback until the surrounding transaction commits; emitAppEvent and the webhook hook use it.

**EmailHandoff**  
{ template, data } returned by a handler's email selector; recipients and sender come from the email registry.

**emitAppEvent**  
emitAppEvent(name, data): builds the actor envelope and runs the registered handler, after commit when inside db.txn().

**findOwnedIntegration**  
Loads an integration by id only if the caller's user or organization owns it.

**Integration**  
A named provider connection owned by a user, organization, OrganizationUser, space or SpaceUser.

**IntegrationRecord**  
Links an Integration to a synced CustomerRef, with poisonedAt for repeated rejections.

**integrations**  
Class: owner Integrations (provider connections) and the IntegrationRecords they sync.

**makeAdapterRouter**  
Picks the provider for process.env.ENVIRONMENT with a default; the standard adapter wrapper.

**makeAppEvent**  
Defines an event handler { email, websocket, cb } whose tasks run isolated with allSettled and aggregated failures.

**makeBroadcastRegistry**  
Registers providers by name and runs an operation on all of them via Promise.allSettled.

**object-storage**  
Class: the env-routed S3 storage client behind the storage adapter, and its buckets.

**observeRegistry**  
Broadcasts every envelope to the structured log and database adapters; best-effort, not a retry queue.

**poisoned record**  
IntegrationRecord.poisonedAt set after 3 receiver rejections (400/422) while other records deliver; later deliveries skip it.

**sendWebhook**  
Job handler delivering one event to one subscription: sign, POST, record, retry.

**storage**  
The exported StorageClient adapter (apps/api/src/lib/storage) routed over createS3Client.

**validateWebhookUrl**  
Rejects unsafe user-supplied target URLs (private addresses, non-enforced envs aside); webhookUrlSchema wraps it for zod.

**webhookEnabledModels**  
Registry of models whose mutations fire outbound webhooks (currently CustomerRef).

**WebhookEvent**  
One delivery attempt: status (pending/sent/failed), payload, HTTP status and response; cleaned after 90 days.

**webhookRelatedModels**  
Maps a model to related records (FlexibleRef) whose changes fire its webhooks.

**webhooks**  
Class: outbound webhooks: subscriptions, signed delivery jobs, delivery history, URL safety, circuit breaker.

**WebhookSubscription**  
A User/Organization/Space-owned URL subscribed to a WebhookModel, unique per owner, model and url, with isActive.

**WSHandoff**  
WebSocket handoff: channels or users message (refetch hints) or a stream append built with streamAppend.

**x-webhook-signature**  
Base64 RSA-SHA256 signature of the timestamped body; receivers verify with the public key.

## 1. What this Warden covers

How the template's code reaches the outside world: business writes emit typed app events whose handlers fan out to email, WebSocket, observation and callbacks after commit; mutations of enabled models fire signed outbound webhooks through jobs; and every external provider (storage, error reporting, messaging) sits behind an adapter module, with owner Integrations recording connections to providers and their synced records.

## 2. The domain

App events are the only way business logic triggers a side effect. A write path calls emitAppEvent(name, data); the name and payload type are declared in apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts (AppEventName) and the handler is built with makeAppEvent({ email, websocket, cb }). emitAppEvent wraps the data in a UUIDv7 envelope with the actor from auditActorContext and, inside db.txn(), defers execution with db.onCommit. makeAppEvent runs observation, each handoff and each callback isolated through db.parallel(…, allSettled). Email handoffs (template + data) go to the sendEmail planner job; WebSocket handoffs go through sendToChannel/sendToUser or, for data streams, an append built with streamAppend; the observe registry always receives the whole envelope and upserts AppEvent best-effort. Heavy or retryable work is enqueued from a cb, never done inline, and nothing synchronous calls an external service from a request.

Webhooks are driven by the mutation hook system, not by app events: a commit on a model in webhookEnabledModels (or a child listed in webhookRelatedModels) makes the webhook hook enqueue one sendWebhook job per active WebhookSubscription, which signs the timestamped body with RSA-SHA256 (x-webhook-signature, public key at /webhookSubscription/info), delivers it, records a WebhookEvent, retries with backoff, auto-disables a subscription after 5 consecutive failures, and on integration subscriptions poisons an IntegrationRecord the receiver keeps rejecting with 400/422. Who may subscribe to what is declared in webhookOwnerAllowedModels; target URLs pass validateWebhookUrl/webhookUrlSchema (SSRF: private addresses refused). Integration is a provider connection owned by a user, organization, membership or space, IntegrationRecord links it to a synced CustomerRef; load integrations through findOwnedIntegration.

Adapters: an adapter module is types.ts (role interface such as StorageClient), client/<provider>.ts (create<Provider><Role> factories taking typed config, no env reads) and index.ts (env reads + wrapping). Choose makeAdapterRouter for one provider per ENVIRONMENT (the default, even with a single provider), makeBroadcastRegistry for fan-out to every provider (messaging; never storage), makeAdapterRegistry when the caller picks by name; email's per-tenant direct factory is the documented exception. No noop providers in the registry, no auth logic in adapters, and app code never imports a provider SDK. Object storage is the storage adapter over createS3Client (MinIO locally). Not here: the email planner, templates and delivery rules (email regions), WebSocket connection and stream machinery itself (websockets), the db hook registry and onCommit internals (mutation-hooks / database), job queues (jobs).

Point at a class when that is as specific as the moment allows, or at a member. Each member: **name** `where`: choose this when … . Where the docs or code give material, a second line describes the hand-rolled code an agent writes when it rebuilds the primitive instead of using it. Code members come from the catalog, described from the code. Doc members are named in the doc sections in part 4. *Also here, by name* lists the parts of a larger system.

### Class `app-events`: emitAppEvent side-effect bus: handlers, handoffs to email/ws/observe, commit deferral

- **AppEvent** `packages/db/prisma/schema/appEvent.prisma`: Event stream for side effects; for before/after mutation diffs use AuditLog instead.
- **emitAppEvent** `apps/api/src/appEvents/emit.ts#emitAppEvent`: Always for email, SMS, analytics, notifications or WebSocket pushes from business logic; never call those services directly.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a controller or service calling the email sender, an SMS/analytics client, enqueue('sendEmail'), or sendToUser/sendToChannel directly after a write (docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md § Purpose and execution; AI/ENTRYPOINT.md § 6 ("Business logic NEVER calls email, SMS, analytics, or notification services directly"))
- **makeAppEvent** `apps/api/src/appEvents/makeAppEvent.ts#makeAppEvent`: Define handlers here; emit with emitAppEvent. Heavy or retryable work: enqueueJob from a cb instead of doing it inline.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-written handler that runs its side effects with a bare Promise.all (one failure cancels the rest) or does heavy/retryable work inline instead of enqueueing a job from a cb (docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md § Purpose and execution; catalog makeAppEvent)
- **Inquiry event definitions per type** `apps/api/src/modules/inquiry/handlers/<type>/appEvents.ts`: inquiry-specific events; general business events go in apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/ instead.
- **Isolated settled side-effect tasks** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Purpose and execution`: Independent side effects that may each open transactions or run inline jobs; sequential when ordering matters.
- **Segment junction diff events** `reconcileSegment / reconcileCustomerRefSegments`: publish membership diffs as owner- and member-side events after reconcile
- **App event channels** `apps/api/src/appEvents/channels/`: bridge app event handoffs to email and WebSocket delivery
- **App event handler registry** `apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/`: Registration alone doesn't prove a writer emits the event; verify an emit call exists.
- **AppEventName** `apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts`: enumerate valid event names typed against their payloads
- **auditActorContext** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Purpose and execution`: supply actor provenance stamped onto event envelopes
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* threading the acting user id through function arguments so a write can be attributed, or setting the actor store directly (docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Audit Log › Actor Context)
- **createSerializedQueue** `APP_EVENTS.md#websocket-handoffs`: in-process ordering; cross-process ownership needs a lock
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a module-level `let pending = Promise.resolve()` chain, a boolean busy flag, or an async-mutex dependency to order writes to one resource (docs/claude/CONCURRENCY.md § Serialized Queue (createSerializedQueue))
- **db.onCommit** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Purpose and execution`: Inside db.txn when work must only happen after commit; emitAppEvent uses it automatically.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* sending email, calling an external API or enqueuing a job directly inside db.txn (so it fires even if the transaction rolls back), or a hand-built after-commit callback list (docs/claude/DATABASE.md § Transactions › After Commit Callbacks; FEATURES.md § Post-Commit Callbacks)
- **db.parallel** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Purpose and execution`: Use allSettled so one failed task doesn't block siblings; failures thrown after settlement.
- **db.txn** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Purpose and execution`: run writes in a transaction whose app events fire on commit
- **deliverEmail** `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/deliverEmail.ts`: actual delivery; planning belongs in sendEmail.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* enqueueJob('deliverEmail', …) from anywhere but the planner (catalog: deliverEmail (enqueued by sendEmail; do not enqueue 'deliverEmail' directly))
- **emit** `apps/api/src/appEvents/emit.ts`: emit typed app events with actor envelope, deferred until transaction commit
- **observe** `apps/api/src/lib/observe.ts`: adapt app event outcomes into observation telemetry
- **observeRegistry** `APP_EVENTS.md#observe-pipeline`: best-effort observation; not a durable retry queue (use jobs)
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* writing AppEvent rows or event analytics logs by hand in a handler, or adding a per-handler observe selector (docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md § Handler and handoff contracts ("no per-handler observe selector") and § Observe pipeline)
- **sendEmail** `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/sendEmail.ts`: planning recipients/template; actual provider send is deliverEmail.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* calling createResendClient(...).send / defaultEmailClient().send from business logic, or enqueuing sendEmail by hand with a recipient list, instead of emitting an app event with an EmailHandoff (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Send Pipeline (event-driven, two BullMQ jobs, never a direct client call; no caller-supplied recipients))
- **No synchronous external calls in requests** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Purpose and execution`: Any controller or write path that would otherwise call a provider inline.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* await fetch(providerUrl) or a provider SDK call inline in a controller or write path (docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md § Purpose and execution ("Nothing synchronous hits an external service"))
- **Observe registry receives every envelope** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Handler and handoff contracts`: When adding analytics or observation of events.
- **Register events in handlers index** `apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts`: Whenever adding a new app event.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* emitting a free-form event string or payload type not declared in AppEventName and the handlers index (docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md § Emitting and registering events)
- **Side effects only through app events** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Purpose and execution`: Any business write path that triggers email, SMS, analytics, notifications or WebSocket pushes.
- **Side effects only via emitAppEvent** `CLAUDE.md §6 App Events & Side Effects`: Any business-logic side effect.
- **Use shared handoff contracts for inquiry events** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#Inquiry events`: Any inquiry sent/resolved event definition.

### Class `webhooks`: Outbound webhooks: subscriptions, signing, delivery jobs, SSRF-safe fetch

- **WebhookEvent** `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookEvent.prisma`: Delivery history per subscription: use this; subscriber endpoint config: WebhookSubscription instead.
- **WebhookSubscription** `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookSubscription.prisma`: Owner is polymorphic via ownerModel plus one of userId/organizationId/spaceId; unique per owner, model and url.
- **registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook** `apps/api/src/hooks/webhookSubscriptionUrl/hook.ts#registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook`: register a db hook that checks WebhookSubscription URL writes
- **sendWebhook** `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/sendWebhook.ts#sendWebhook`: Normally enqueued by the webhook hook per subscription; don't call providers or fetch directly.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* fetch()/POST to subscriber URLs from a controller, hook or app-event cb, with signing and retry hand-rolled (catalog sendWebhook; docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks, How It Works)
- **validateWebhookUrl** `apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/validators/validateWebhookUrl.ts#validateWebhookUrl`: Use this for any user-supplied target URL; isPrivateAddress and hostnameOf are its building blocks.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* hand-rolled localhost/10.x/169.254 checks, or no check at all, before fetching a user-supplied URL (catalog validateWebhookUrl ("Use this for any user-supplied target URL"))
- **webhookEnabledModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/enabledModels.ts#webhookEnabledModels`: list models whose mutations emit outbound webhooks (currently CustomerRef)
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a custom after-mutation hook or app-event cb that looks up subscriptions and enqueues deliveries for a model, instead of adding the model to webhookEnabledModels (docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks, Enabling Webhooks for a Model)
- **webhookModelSubscribers** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/ownerAllowedModels.ts#webhookModelSubscribers`: Inverse of webhookOwnerAllowedModels; use when starting from the changed model rather than the owner.
- **webhookOwnerAllowedModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/ownerAllowedModels.ts#webhookOwnerAllowedModels`: Edit here to allow a new subscription; read webhookModelSubscribers for model-to-owner lookups, webhookRelatedModels for related-record fan-out.
- **webhookRelatedModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/relatedModels.ts#webhookRelatedModels`: Use for polymorphic related-record matching; webhookOwnerAllowedModels only lists permitted subscription models.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* extra code that fires a parent's webhook when a child record changes (docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks, Related Models)
- **webhookUrlSchema** `apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription/schemas/webhookSubscriptionSchemas.ts#webhookUrlSchema`: Schema-level URL input checks; call validateWebhookUrl directly outside zod parsing.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* url: z.string().url() on a webhook subscription body (catalog webhookUrlSchema)
- **apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription** `apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription`: Managing an existing subscription; creation goes through me/organization/space CreateWebhookSubscription endpoints.
- **Webhook circuit breaker** `docs/claude/HOOKS.md > Webhooks > Circuit Breaker`: general delivery failures; repeated 400/422 for one record on integration subscriptions poisons the record instead
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* custom failure counters or flags that disable a subscription after repeated delivery failures (docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks, Circuit Breaker)
- **Webhooks enqueued on commit** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#Webhooks`: send outbound webhooks via sendWebhook job after transaction commits
- **Webhooks fire after commit via hooks** `FEATURES.md › Webhooks`: never send inline in the request or inside the transaction
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* sending a webhook inline in the request or inside the transaction (FEATURES.md › Webhooks (Event-Based Triggers))
- **truncateWebhookSubscriptions** `packages/db/prisma/truncateWebhookSubscriptions.ts`: Already run by clone.sh; use standalone only on local/test DBs.
- **webhooks** `apps/api/src/hooks/index.ts`: deliver outbound webhooks post-commit after mutations
- **x-webhook-signature** `FEATURES.md › Webhooks`: sign timestamped webhook bodies with RSA-SHA256 for receiver verification
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an HMAC with a per-subscription shared secret, or unsigned/untimestamped webhook bodies (FEATURES.md › Webhooks (RSA Signature Verification))
- *Also here, by name:* WEBHOOK_NOOP_FIELDS (`packages/db/src/registries/redactFields.ts`); WebhookEventAction (`packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookEvent.prisma`); WebhookEventStatus (`packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookEvent.prisma`); WebhookModel (`packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookSubscription.prisma`); WebhookOwnerModel (`packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookSubscription.prisma`); WebhooksPage (`packages/ui/src/pages/WebhooksPage.tsx`); hostnameOf (`apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/validators/hostnameOf.ts`); isEnforcedEnvironment (`apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/validators/isEnforcedEnvironment.ts`); isPrivateAddress (`apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/validators/isPrivateAddress.ts`); webhookSubscriptionCreateBodySchema (`apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription/schemas/webhookSubscriptionSchemas.ts`); webhookSubscriptionReadResponseSchema (`apps/api/src/modules/webhookSubscription/schemas/webhookSubscriptionSchemas.ts`)

### Class `adapters`: Provider adapter modules: one interface over provider implementations (makeAdapterRouter/Registry)

- **makeAdapterRegistry** `packages/shared/src/adapter/registry.ts#makeAdapterRegistry`: Selecting one adapter by key; fan-out to all: makeBroadcastRegistry; selecting by ENVIRONMENT: makeAdapterRouter.
- **makeAdapterRouter** `packages/shared/src/adapter/router.ts#makeAdapterRouter`: Per-environment provider selection, even with one provider; keyed lookup: makeAdapterRegistry; fan-out: makeBroadcastRegistry.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* an adapter index.ts exporting a provider directly, or if (process.env.ENVIRONMENT === 'prod') provider switches in app code (docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md § Adapter primitives and § What NOT to do)
- **makeBroadcastRegistry** `packages/shared/src/adapter/broadcast.ts#makeBroadcastRegistry`: Fan-out to several providers; one provider picked by key: makeAdapterRegistry; per-environment choice: makeAdapterRouter. Never for storage.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a hand-written loop over providers with Promise.allSettled to send one message on every channel (docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md § Adapter primitives (makeBroadcastRegistry))
- **Adapter module for external services** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#What an adapter module is`: Wrap when external service, env-divergent impl, clean test mocking, or plausible second provider; otherwise import the library directly.
- **Direct factory for per-tenant email client** `packages/email/src/client/`: Provider chosen per call/tenant; makeAdapterRouter when chosen once per environment.
- **errorReporter** `apps/api/src/lib/errorReporter/`: report errors via console or Sentry selected per environment
- **messageProviderRegistry** `apps/api/src/lib/messaging/providers.ts`: broadcast a message across all registered communication channel providers
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a switch on contact.type that calls Twilio or another SDK inline for SMS/push (docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md § Messaging › Provider Registry and § SMS (register a MessageProviderAdapter under the ContactType))
- **storage** `apps/api/src/lib/storage/`: provide the env-routed S3 object storage client to application code
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* importing @aws-sdk/* or presigning URLs by hand in a module instead of calling the storage adapter (docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md § What an adapter module is and § Existing examples)
- **Adapter client singleton shape** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#What NOT to do`: Map<config, client> only for per-tenant configs like email resend.
- **Adapter module layout** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#Module layout`: All new adapter modules, even single-provider ones (three files minimum).
- **Adapter naming conventions** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#Naming conventions`: All adapter modules.
- **Always wrap index.ts export in makeAdapterRouter** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#What NOT to do`: Env-selected adapters; email's per-tenant direct factory is the documented exception.
- **Double-underscore private prefix** `docs/claude/NAMING.md#underscore-prefix`: Private module-level state; use _ only for unused parameters.
- **Env reads only in adapter index.ts** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#What NOT to do`: All adapter provider files.
- **Never import provider SDKs in app code** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#What an adapter module is`: Any service wrapped by an adapter module.
- **No auth logic in adapters** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#What NOT to do`: Any adapter module.
- **No noop registered adapters** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#What NOT to do`: Testing code that uses an adapter.

### Class `integrations`: Owner integrations and their synced records

- **Integration** `packages/db/prisma/schema/integration.prisma`: synced external items: IntegrationRecord instead; credentials live on Token
- **IntegrationRecord** `packages/db/prisma/schema/integrationRecord.prisma`: the connection itself: Integration instead; external identity relation: CustomerRef
- **findOwnedIntegration** `apps/api/src/modules/integration/services/findOwnedIntegration.ts#findOwnedIntegration`: Use instead of raw prisma findUnique on integrations so ownership scope is enforced.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* db.integration.findUnique({ where: { id } }) in a controller with no ownership scope (catalog findOwnedIntegration)
- **integrationProviders** `packages/ui/src/lib/integrationProviders.ts#integrationProviders`: Use for provider display metadata; customIntegration covers custom integrations without a provider.
- **IntegrationsPage** `packages/ui/src/pages/IntegrationsPage.tsx#IntegrationsPage`: Use instead of opening CreateIntegrationModal directly; it owns provider buckets from lib/integrationProviders.ts.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* a new settings page that renders CreateIntegrationModal directly and re-buckets providers itself (catalog IntegrationsPage)
- **isIntegrationRecordPoisoned** `apps/api/src/modules/integration/services/isIntegrationRecordPoisoned.ts#isIntegrationRecordPoisoned`: Read check; poisonIntegrationRecord marks a record poisoned.
- **poisonIntegrationRecord** `apps/api/src/modules/integration/services/poisonIntegrationRecord.ts#poisonIntegrationRecord`: Writes the poison mark; isIntegrationRecordPoisoned to check it before delivery.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* custom per-record rejection counting or skip lists for integration webhook deliveries (docs/claude/HOOKS.md § Webhooks, Poisoned Records)
- **apps/api/src/modules/integration** `apps/api/src/modules/integration`: read, update and delete integrations, with a superadmin listing
- *Also here, by name:* INTEGRATION_IMMUTABLE_FIELDS (`apps/api/src/modules/integration/schemas/integrationSchemas.ts`); IntegrationOwnerModel (`packages/db/prisma/schema/integration.prisma`); Provider (`packages/db/prisma/schema/integration.prisma`); customIntegration (`packages/ui/src/lib/integrationProviders.ts`); integrationCreateBodySchema (`apps/api/src/modules/integration/schemas/integrationSchemas.ts`); integrationProviderValues (`packages/ui/src/lib/integrationProviders.ts`); integrationReadResponseSchema (`apps/api/src/modules/integration/schemas/integrationSchemas.ts`); integrationRecordColumn (`apps/api/src/modules/integration/services/integrationRecordColumn.ts`); integrationUpdateBodySchema (`apps/api/src/modules/integration/schemas/integrationSchemas.ts`)

### Class `object-storage`: Object storage client (S3) behind the adapter

- **createS3Client** `apps/api/src/lib/storage/client/s3.ts#createS3Client`: Use instead of instantiating S3Client from the AWS SDK directly.
  - *Signs you're bypassing it:* new S3Client(...) from @aws-sdk/client-s3 instantiated in application code (catalog createS3Client; docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md § What an adapter module is ("never a provider SDK directly"))
- **scripts/db/minio-provision.sh** `scripts/db/minio-provision.sh`: Removing buckets: minio-remove.sh.
- **scripts/db/minio-remove.sh** `scripts/db/minio-remove.sh`: remove MinIO buckets, reporting each, on worktree teardown

## 4. The specifics, in full

### 4a. Doc sections

Each unit is the doc section verbatim, with its headings shifted down two levels. A source line above it gives the path, the section and the doc's H1.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#purpose-and-execution -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Purpose and execution (in "App Events")

#### Purpose and execution

Business logic never calls email, SMS, analytics, or notification services directly; every side
effect goes through an app event. Direct calls couple every controller to every channel and put
provider outages in the request path. Nothing synchronous hits an external service.

Business write paths emit events; handlers select side effects. Email delivery runs in jobs,
WebSocket handoffs use Redis pub/sub, and observation records the event envelope. This keeps
delivery logic out of controllers and lets each consumer evolve independently.

`emitAppEvent(name, data)` creates a UUIDv7 envelope with actor provenance from
`auditActorContext` and dispatches the registered handler. Inside `db.txn()`, execution is
registered with `db.onCommit`; outside a transaction, the handler is awaited immediately.

`makeAppEvent` executes observation, each email/WebSocket handoff, and each callback through
`db.parallel(tasks, { resolution: 'allSettled' })`. Each task gets its own database async scope.
A failed task does not prevent siblings from running; collected failures are thrown after
settlement. This isolation matters when a callback starts a transaction or runs a test-mode job
inline while the observe adapter also writes.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#emitting-and-registering-events -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Emitting and registering events (in "App Events")

#### Emitting and registering events

```typescript
import { emitAppEvent } from '#/appEvents';

await emitAppEvent('user.verificationRequested', {
  userId: user.id,
  verificationUrl,
});
```

Event names and payload types are declared in `apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/index.ts`.
Add the payload, `AppEventName` entry and handler registration there. Each handler lives in
its feature folder and is constructed with `makeAppEvent`:

```typescript
export const userVerificationRequested = makeAppEvent<UserVerificationRequestedPayload>({
  email: (data) => [{
    template: 'email-verification',
    data: { userId: data.userId, verificationUrl: data.verificationUrl },
  }],
});
```

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#handler-and-handoff-contracts -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Handler and handoff contracts (in "App Events")

#### Handler and handoff contracts

```typescript
type EmailHandoff = {
  template: string;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
};

type WSChannelsHandoff = {
  kind: 'channels';
  target: { channels: string[] };
  message: { data: Record<string, unknown> };
};

type WSUsersHandoff = {
  kind: 'users';
  target: { userIds: string[] };
  message: { data: Record<string, unknown> };
};

type WSStreamAppendHandoff = {
  kind: 'stream';
  target: { stream: string; userIds?: string[] };
  append: { type: string; payload: unknown };
};

type WSHandoff = WSChannelsHandoff | WSUsersHandoff | WSStreamAppendHandoff;

type AppEventHandlerDefinition<T> = {
  email?: (data: T) => EmailHandoff[] | null;
  websocket?: (data: T) => WSHandoff[] | null;
  cb?: Array<(data: T) => Promise<void> | void>;
};
```

There is no per-handler `observe` selector: the complete envelope is always sent to the
observe registry. Sender, recipients and delivery policy are defined by the email registry,
not supplied as `to`/`cc`/`bcc` on an event's email handoff.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#email-pipeline -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Email pipeline (in "App Events")

#### Email pipeline

`deliverEmailHandoffs` enqueues `sendEmail` with the template, event name and binding data,
using a deterministic planner job ID. The registry entry in `apps/api/src/lib/email/registry.ts`
defines the entity lens, sender, recipient rules, data lens and render policy.

The planner resolves entity/sender/template ownership, hydrates recipients through the
owner-scoped recipient lens, and creates or reuses a `CommunicationLog` row per recipient
using its idempotency key. It then enqueues `deliverEmail`. Delivery settles the template and
its component versions, applies contact preferences and address verification, renders and
sends, and records the result. See [COMMUNICATIONS.md](COMMUNICATIONS.md#planner-sendemail)
for the complete planner/delivery and degraded-rule behavior.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#websocket-handoffs -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § WebSocket handoffs (in "App Events")

#### WebSocket handoffs

Channel-targeted example, from `segmentMembersAdded`:

```typescript
websocket: (data) => [{
  target: { channels: [WS_CHANNELS.segmentReadManySegmentMembers.name(data.segmentId)] },
  message: { data: refetch({ _id: 'segmentReadManySegmentMembers', path: { id: data.segmentId } }) },
}],
```

`deliverWSHandoffs` sends a message handoff through `sendToChannel` or `sendToUser`, and a
stream handoff through `appendToStream`. The frontend handles query-refetch hints and
data-stream actions. New payload kinds require their own consumer and recovery design.
Subscription and stream-open checks use the underlying authorized route; see
[WEBSOCKETS.md](WEBSOCKETS.md).

Stream handoffs are never built by hand. `streamAppend` (`apps/api/src/appEvents/streamAppend.ts`)
takes a shared stream definition, its params, an op and a payload. The op must be one the
definition's kind defines (`list`: `upsert`, `remove`; `log`: `append`), the payload is typed by
that op, and the options argument carries `revive` (upserts only: may restore a removed row) and,
for a `perRecipient` definition, the required recipient `userIds`. An upsert row must come from
`routeRow(route, value)`, which parses it with the route's own `responseSchema` exactly as the
route's response is. From the
contact handlers (the scaffolding example stream):

```typescript
websocket: ({ contact }) => organizationContactRemove(contact),

// organizationContactRemove:
streamAppend(STREAM_DEFINITIONS.organizationReadManyContacts, { id: contact.organizationId }, 'remove', {
  id: contact.id,
});
```

A `shared` stream's append goes to every connection holding the stream, so it has to match the
shape of the route's response for every caller. `appendToStream` publishes each stream's appends
through a per-stream `createSerializedQueue`, so one instance emits them in order. See
[WEBSOCKETS.md](WEBSOCKETS.md#data-streams).

Revoking access (membership, role or token removal) does not yet emit an app event that closes
streams immediately; the periodic re-authorization in
[WEBSOCKETS.md](WEBSOCKETS.md#authorization-and-re-authorization) closes them within one
interval.

Segments also publish member-side `customerRef.segmentsAdded` / `customerRef.segmentsRemoved`
events. For User customers those target the user's sockets with a membership-query refetch.
See [SEGMENTS.md](SEGMENTS.md#events-and-email-integration).

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#observe-pipeline -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Observe pipeline (in "App Events")

#### Observe pipeline

The envelope contains `id`, `name`, `actor` and `data`. Observation broadcasts it through
`observeRegistry` to the structured log and database adapters. The database adapter directly
upserts `AppEvent` by envelope ID. This is idempotent, best-effort observation, not a durable
retry queue. The event ID encodes emit time; observation is not a separate BullMQ job.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#inquiry-events -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Inquiry events (in "App Events")

#### Inquiry events

Inquiry-specific definitions live under `apps/api/src/modules/inquiry/handlers/<type>/appEvents.ts`.
The central inquiry event handlers delegate to those definitions. For example, the
organization-invitation `sent` definition selects `inquiry-invite-organization-user` with
`{ inquiryId }` bindings and publishes an `inquiryRead` refetch. Its `resolved` definition
publishes the refetch. Use the shared handoff contracts for both.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md#source-map-and-pending-consumers -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` § Source map and pending consumers (in "App Events")

#### Source map and pending consumers

- `apps/api/src/appEvents/emit.ts`: typed emit, actor envelope and commit deferral.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/makeAppEvent.ts`: task isolation and failure aggregation.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/types.ts`: envelope, handoffs and handler definition.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/channels/`: email and WebSocket delivery bridges.
- `apps/api/src/appEvents/handlers/`: business-event handlers and the registry.
- `apps/api/src/lib/observe.ts`: observation adapters.
- `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/sendEmail.ts`, `deliverEmail.ts`: email planner and delivery.

Feature flags and persisted in-app notifications remain future consumers. Registering an event
handler does not prove that a business writer emits the event; the Segments documentation
lists the reconciliation events still waiting for production write paths.

<!-- unit doc:AI/ENTRYPOINT.md#6-app-events-side-effects -->
**Source:** `AI/ENTRYPOINT.md` § 6. App Events & Side Effects (in "AI ENTRYPOINT")

#### 6. App Events & Side Effects

Business logic NEVER calls email, SMS, analytics, or notification services directly. All side effects go through `emitAppEvent`. Read `docs/claude/APP_EVENTS.md` before modifying the event system.

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md#webhooks -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/COMMUNICATIONS.md` § Webhooks (in "Communications")

#### Webhooks

Existing webhook system. See [HOOKS.md](HOOKS.md) for webhook delivery.

```typescript
// Current: webhooks sent via sendWebhook job
db.onCommit(() => enqueue('sendWebhook', { ... }));
```

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/HOOKS.md#webhooks -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/HOOKS.md` § Webhooks (in "Hooks")

#### Webhooks

Automatic webhook delivery on database mutations.

##### Enabling Webhooks for a Model

```typescript
// packages/db/src/registries/webhook/enabledModels.ts
export const webhookEnabledModels: WebhookModel[] = [
  WebhookModel.CustomerRef,
];
```

##### How It Works

1. DB mutation triggers `webhookDelivery` hook (after commit)
2. Hook finds active subscriptions for the model
3. Enqueues `sendWebhook` job for each subscription
4. Job signs payload with RSA-SHA256 and delivers

##### Webhook Payload

```typescript
{
  model: 'User',
  action: 'create' | 'update' | 'delete',
  resourceId: '...',
  data: { ...fields },
  previousData: { ...fields },  // For updates only
  timestamp: '2024-01-15T12:00:00.000Z'
}
```

Headers: `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Webhook-Signature: <base64>`

##### Circuit Breaker

After 5 consecutive failures, subscription auto-disables:

```typescript
const FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 5;
// If last 5 events all failed → isActive = false
```

##### Poisoned Records

On a subscription with an `integrationId`, one record the receiver keeps rejecting is poisoned
instead of tripping the circuit. A rejection is an `error` event with `httpStatus` 400 or 422
(`RECORD_REJECTION` in `sendWebhook.ts`). Other terminal failures such as redirects, 401, 403 or 429
do not count, and neither does `unreachable`. When a record has 3 rejections since its own last
success, and some other record has delivered since the first of them, `poisonIntegrationRecord`
stamps `IntegrationRecord.poisonedAt`. Later deliveries of that record are skipped before signing,
with no `WebhookEvent` and nothing fed to the circuit. Nothing clears the stamp yet. See
`tickets/INFRA-032-webhook-poisoned-records.md`.

##### Ignored Fields

`HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS` is the **shared** ignore registry — used by audit, cache, webhooks, and the generic `isNoOpUpdate`. Any field listed here is:

1. **Excluded from payload** - never sent to webhook subscribers
2. **Stripped before audit diff** - changes don't produce AuditLog entries
3. **Treated as a no-op** - updates that only touch ignored fields skip the cache/webhook/audit hooks

```typescript
// packages/db/src/registries/ignoreFields.ts
const HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS_BASE: Record<string, string[]> = {
  _global: ['updatedAt'],      // Always ignored for all models
  User: ['lastLoginAt'],       // Login timestamp not meaningful
  Token: ['lastUsedAt'],       // Token usage timestamp not meaningful
};

// Auto-composes from encryption + orderedList registries so encrypted column
// triplets (encryptedX / encryptedXMetadata / encryptedXKeyVersion) and
// ordered-list position fields don't need to be re-listed per model.
export const HOOK_IGNORE_FIELDS = buildHookIgnoreFields();
```

Use cases:
- **Timestamps** (`updatedAt`, `lastUsedAt`) - noisy, not meaningful
- **Sensitive data** (encrypted blobs) - auto-composed from encryption registry
- **Presentation-only state** (ordered-list `position`) - auto-composed from orderedList registry; the `orderedList` hook owns cache invalidation for ordering cascades (see [Ordered List](#ordered-list))

##### Related Models

Child models can trigger parent webhooks:

```typescript
// packages/db/src/registries/webhook/relatedModels.ts
export const webhookRelatedModels: Record<string, FlexibleRef[]> = {
  User: [{ model: 'CustomerRef', axis: 'customerModel', value: 'User' }],
};
```

---

<!-- unit doc:FEATURES.md#webhooks -->
**Source:** `FEATURES.md` § Webhooks (in "Template Features")

#### Webhooks

**Event-Driven Integration System** - Notify external systems when data changes. Organizations/spaces subscribe to events, receive RSA-SHA256-signed payloads. Automatic retries, delivery tracking, and async processing via job queue.

- ✅ **Webhook Subscriptions** - Organizations and spaces can subscribe to events (user.created, organization.updated, etc.). Each subscription has URL, events list, and active/inactive status. Payloads are signed with a server-held RSA private key (asymmetric); receivers verify with the published public key. False polymorphism pattern allows User/Organization/Space ownership

- ✅ **Event-Based Triggers** - Database hooks automatically fire webhook deliveries after successful mutations. Hook system ensures webhooks only sent after transaction commits. Events follow pattern: `{resource}.{action}` (user.created, token.deleted)

- ✅ **RSA Signature Verification** - Each webhook includes `x-webhook-signature` header with an RSA-SHA256 signature (base64). Signed with a server-held private key; receivers verify with the public key exposed at `/webhookSubscription/info`. Asymmetric — no shared secret to leak. Signed body includes a unix `timestamp` so receivers can reject replays. Prevents webhook spoofing and tampering

- ✅ **Async Delivery via Jobs** - Webhooks enqueued as BullMQ jobs on the shared `jobs` queue. Never blocks request processing. Failed deliveries retry automatically (3 attempts, exponential backoff). Webhook jobs run outside transaction to avoid timeouts

- ✅ **Delivery Tracking** - WebhookEvent model records every delivery attempt with status (pending, sent, failed), response code, response body, error message. Superadmins can inspect delivery history and debug integration issues

- ✅ **Automatic Cleanup** - Cron job removes old webhook events (90+ days) to prevent unbounded table growth. Configurable retention period

- ✅ **Superadmin Oversight** - Superadmin routes for viewing all subscriptions across organizations, inspecting delivery failures, manually retriggering failed deliveries

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#what-an-adapter-module-is -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md` § What an adapter module is (in "Adapter Modules")

#### What an adapter module is

An adapter module exposes **one stable interface** to application code, and wraps one or more **provider implementations** behind it. Application code imports the interface — never a provider SDK directly.

Three concerns inside an adapter module:

1. **Interface (`types.ts`)** — what the application expects (e.g. `StorageClient.presignPost`). Provider-agnostic.
2. **Provider(s) (`client/<name>.ts`)** — concrete implementations of the interface (e.g. `createS3Client`). One file per provider.
3. **Wiring (`index.ts`)** — reads env vars, constructs providers, wraps in an adapter primitive, exports the chosen instance.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#module-layout -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md` § Module layout (in "Adapter Modules")

#### Module layout

This is the canonical structure. All new adapter modules follow it.

```
<moduleName>/
├── index.ts              # env reads + makeAdapterRouter → exports the adapter
├── types.ts              # The interface (role-based name: ErrorReporter, StorageClient, EmailClient)
└── client/
    ├── <provider1>.ts    # createXClient(config) — implements the interface
    └── <provider2>.ts    # createYClient(config) — alternate provider
```

Why `client/` as a subfolder:
- Pre-creates the seam for additional providers without restructuring.
- Single-provider modules sit in `client/` alone; the pattern doesn't change when a second provider lands.
- Matches `packages/email/src/client/` (the most recently refined example).

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#adapter-primitives -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md` § Adapter primitives (in "Adapter Modules")

#### Adapter primitives

All in `@template/shared/adapter`. Pick based on selection semantics.

##### makeAdapterRouter — pick-one per environment

Use when: **one provider runs per environment**. The router selects by `process.env.ENVIRONMENT`. This is the default — most adapter modules.

```typescript
import { makeAdapterRouter } from '@template/shared/adapter';
import { createS3Client } from '#/lib/storage/client/s3';
import type { StorageClient } from '#/lib/storage/types';

const s3 = createS3Client({ /* env-derived config */ });

export const storage = makeAdapterRouter<StorageClient>({
  prod: s3,
  staging: s3,
  pr: s3,
  default: s3,
});
```

Even with a single provider, route through `makeAdapterRouter`. The seam exists for future env-divergent behavior (e.g., `test: noopStorage` later) without touching application code.

##### makeBroadcastRegistry — fan-out across providers

Use when: **a single operation should hit multiple providers in parallel**. E.g., a message dispatched across all registered communication channels.

```typescript
import { makeBroadcastRegistry } from '@template/shared/adapter';

export const messageProviderRegistry = makeBroadcastRegistry<MessageProviderAdapter>();
// Providers register themselves at load:
messageProviderRegistry.register('email', emailAdapter);
messageProviderRegistry.register('sms', smsAdapter);
// Caller: messageProviderRegistry.broadcast(...) → all providers run via Promise.allSettled
```

Storage is not a fan-out concern — never use `makeBroadcastRegistry` for storage.

##### makeAdapterRegistry — named map

Use when: **caller explicitly picks which provider** by name (not env-derived). Rare. See `packages/shared/src/adapter/registry.ts`.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#naming-conventions -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md` § Naming conventions (in "Adapter Modules")

#### Naming conventions

| Element | Convention | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Module folder | camelCase, role-suffixed | `errorReporter/`, `storage/`, `email/client/` |
| Interface type | Role-based, PascalCase | `ErrorReporter`, `StorageClient`, `EmailClient` |
| Provider factory | `create<Provider><Role>` | `createS3Client`, `createResendClient`, `createConsoleReporter` |
| Exported adapter | Module name (no role suffix) | `errorReporter`, `storage` |
| Module-level singleton | `__` prefix | `let __client: S3Client \| null = null` |

The `__` prefix is the template-wide convention for **internal/private** items (see [NAMING.md](NAMING.md#underscore-prefix)). Never use a single `_` prefix for private — single `_` means "unused" in this codebase.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#existing-examples -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md` § Existing examples (in "Adapter Modules")

#### Existing examples

| Module | Path | Primitive | Providers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Error reporting | `apps/api/src/lib/errorReporter/` | `makeAdapterRouter` | console, sentry |
| Storage | `apps/api/src/lib/storage/` | `makeAdapterRouter` | s3 (only) |
| Email | `packages/email/src/client/` | direct factory | console, resend |
| Messaging providers | `apps/api/src/lib/messaging/providers.ts` | `makeBroadcastRegistry` | per-channel |

Email uses a direct factory (`createConsoleClient`/`createResendClient`) instead of `makeAdapterRouter` because consumers pick the provider explicitly per email (different tenant orgs can have different API keys). Storage and errorReporter pick once per environment — hence the router.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#when-to-create-a-new-adapter-module -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md` § When to create a new adapter module (in "Adapter Modules")

#### When to create a new adapter module

Wrap behind an adapter if any of the following:
- The thing talks to an **external service** (SaaS API, cloud SDK, third-party network resource)
- The implementation might **change per environment** (prod vs local vs test)
- You'd want to **mock it cleanly in tests**
- Another provider for the same role is plausible within 12 months

If none apply, skip the abstraction — just import the library directly. Adapters cost reading-cost; only pay it when there's a real swap concern.

---

<!-- unit doc:docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md#what-not-to-do -->
**Source:** `docs/claude/ADAPTERS.md` § What NOT to do (in "Adapter Modules")

#### What NOT to do

- **Don't bake env reads into provider files.** Env vars belong in the module's `index.ts` only. Providers receive a typed config object.
- **Don't return a direct provider from `index.ts`.** Wrap through `makeAdapterRouter` for env-keyed selection, even if all envs map to the same provider today. The seam is the point.
- **Don't add a `noop` adapter as a registered provider.** Mocks belong at the interface level via `vi.mock()`. A `noop` adapter in the production registry is dishonest — production code could accidentally select it.
- **Don't include auth/permission logic in adapters.** Adapters are mechanical — they sign URLs, send bytes, talk to APIs. Policy (who can call what) lives at the route/middleware layer where permix is wired.
- **Don't use a `Map<config, client>` singleton when there's only one config.** That pattern (see `packages/email/src/client/resend.ts`) exists because email supports per-tenant API keys. For single-config adapters (storage, errorReporter), a plain `let __client = null` module-level singleton is correct.
- **Don't mix concerns into a single file.** Interface in `types.ts`, providers in `client/`, wiring in `index.ts`. Three files minimum, even for a single-provider module.

### 4b. Code entries

From the catalog (`.foundry/catalog/catalog.json`, extracted from the code). Each line: **name** `where` [kind] the job it does. Use: canonical usage.

#### Class `app-events`
- **AppEvent** `packages/db/prisma/schema/appEvent.prisma` [model] record emitted app events with actor, source and JSON payload Use: db.appEvent.findMany({ where: { name } })
- **emitAppEvent** `apps/api/src/appEvents/emit.ts#emitAppEvent` [primitive] trigger all side effects of a domain change, deferred until transaction commit Use: await emitAppEvent('contactCreated', { contact })
- **makeAppEvent** `apps/api/src/appEvents/makeAppEvent.ts#makeAppEvent` [primitive] define an app event handler running observation, email, WebSocket and callbacks in isolation Use: export const myEvent = makeAppEvent<MyPayload>({ email: (d) => [...], cb: [async (d) => {...}] });

#### Class `webhooks`
- **WebhookEvent** `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookEvent.prisma` [model] record each outbound webhook delivery attempt with status, payload and HTTP result Use: db.webhookEvent.findMany({ where: { webhookSubscriptionId, status } })
- **WebhookSubscription** `packages/db/prisma/schema/webhookSubscription.prisma` [model] register a user, organization or space URL to receive webhooks for a model Use: db.webhookSubscription.create({ data: { model, url, ownerModel, organizationId } })
- **registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook** `apps/api/src/hooks/webhookSubscriptionUrl/hook.ts#registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook` [primitive] register a db hook that checks WebhookSubscription URL writes Use: registerWebhookSubscriptionUrlHook(); // at startup with the other db hooks
- **sendWebhook** `apps/api/src/jobs/handlers/sendWebhook.ts#sendWebhook` [primitive] deliver one webhook event to one subscription Use: enqueue sendWebhook with { subscriptionId, action, resourceId, data, timestamp }
- **validateWebhookUrl** `apps/api/src/lib/webhooks/validators/validateWebhookUrl.ts#validateWebhookUrl` [primitive] reject unsafe user-supplied webhook URLs before sending, throwing an app error Use: validateWebhookUrl(url); // optional { enforce: false }
- **webhookEnabledModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/enabledModels.ts#webhookEnabledModels` [primitive] list models whose mutations emit outbound webhooks (currently CustomerRef) Use: webhookEnabledModels.includes(WebhookModel.CustomerRef)
- **webhookModelSubscribers** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/ownerAllowedModels.ts#webhookModelSubscribers` [primitive] look up which owner models may subscribe to webhooks for a given model Use: webhookModelSubscribers[WebhookModel.CustomerRef] // owner models allowed
- **webhookOwnerAllowedModels** `packages/db/src/registries/webhook/ownerAllowedModels.ts#webhookOwnerAllowedModels` [primitive] declare which models each webhook owner (User, Organization, Space) may subscribe to Use: webhookOwnerAllowedModels[WebhookOwnerModel.Organization]
